question: What does SARFAESI mean?
answer:
**SARFAESI** stands for the **Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002**.

It is an Indian law that allows banks and financial institutions to recover non-performing assets (NPAs) — i.e., bad loans — **without going to court**. Under this Act, lenders are empowered to seize and auction residential or commercial properties that were offered as security when a borrower defaults on a loan.

**Sources:**
- [Bajaj Finserv — SARFAESI Act 2002](https://www.bajajfinserv.in/sarfaesi-act)
- [Aditya Birla Capital — SARFAESI Act 2002: Complete Guide](https://www.adityabirlacapital.com/abc-of-money/sarfaesi-act-2002)
- [IBC Law — Procedure for Sale of Immovable Assets under SARFAESI Act 2002](https://ibclaw.in/procedure-for-sale-of-immovable-assets-under-sarfaesi-act-2002)

This is why the properties in this platform are referred to as "SARFAESI auctions" — they are assets being sold by lenders to recover defaulted loans.

question: Explain what EMD is in a bank auction
answer:
**EMD stands for Earnest Money Deposit.** It is the upfront, refundable deposit that a bidder must pay to participate in a bank property auction under the SARFAESI Act.

Key details from the search results:

- **Purpose:** EMD proves you are a serious bidder and secures your participation in the auction.
- **Amount:** Typically **10% of the reserve price** (the minimum price the bank will accept).
- **Refundable:** Yes, it is refundable (e.g., to unsuccessful bidders).

Sources supporting this:
- xpertarc.com: "EMD is typically 10% of reserve price for SARFAESI and DRT auctions."
- auctiondunia.com: "the refundable deposit amount that interested bidders must pay to participate (usually about 10% of the reserve price)."
- legiscore.in: "the refundable security deposit, usually 10% of the reserve price, that you pay to prove you're a serious bidder."

**Takeaway:** If you see an auction listed on the platform, the EMD will almost always be 10% of the reserve price. You must pay this before you can place a bid.

question: What are the RBI guidelines for e-auction of secured assets?
answer:
Based on the search results, here is a summary of the RBI guidelines and procedures for e-auctions of secured assets under the SARFAESI Act:

- **Governing Framework:** The procedure for the sale of immovable assets is laid down under **Rule 8 and 9 of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002**, which are part of the SARFAESI Act, 2002 [ibclaw.in].
- **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP):** A Standard Operating Procedure for the sale of assets under the SARFAESI Act outlines key steps, including issuing demand notices, obtaining asset valuations, and inviting public participation in auctions as per RBI guidelines [scribd.com].
- **Modes of Sale:** Permitted modes of sale include obtaining quotes, inviting tenders, public auctions, and private treaties [scribd.com].
- **Reserve Price:** The procedures for public auctions/tenders include fixing a reserve price in consultation with relevant parties [scribd.com].
- **Sale Certificate:** Upon confirmation of a sale, the creditor must issue a sale certificate in favor of the auction purchaser [ibclaw.in].
- **Right to Redeem:** The borrower has the right to pay the dues at any time before the date of publication of the notice for public auction. If this happens, the secured assets shall not be transferred [indiacode.nic.in].

**Sources:**
- [scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/641931998/SOP-for-Sale-of-Assets-final)
- [ibclaw.in](https://ibclaw.in/procedure-for-sale-of-immovable-assets-under-sarfaesi-act-2002)
- [indiacode.nic.in](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2006/1/A2002-54.pdf)
